title: cedar-lane-telecom-integration-call-notes-2026-02-25
body:
Attendees:
- Rajan Mehta (Redwood CS)
- Sofia Alvarez (Redwood Solutions)
- Miguel Torres (Redwood SRE)
- Priya Nair (Cedar Lane Telecom, Integration Lead)
- Daniel Cho (Cedar Lane, Platform)

Purpose: kickoff integration for Cedar Lane Telecom (CLT) to use Redwood for live support summarization + routing. They want a hybrid approach: hosted API for pilot, Dedicated / Private when SLA/PII requirements kick in.

Summary of ask / requirements (from CLT):
- Primary use case: real-time chat summarization + intent extraction for live agent assist and automated routing.
- Latency target: end-to-end response < 400ms 95th for short summaries (<= 120 tokens). They emphasized perceived latency for agent UI.
- Throughput: peak of ~450 concurrent agents, average request size small (prompt + last 4 messages), expected 30k requests/day initially, ramp to ~300k/day in 6 months.
- Data residency & security: must remain in EU region for EU customers. For US customers, they need SOC2 + KMS key control.
- Retention: CLT policy is 7 days ephemeral for session context; transcripts must be stored centrally in CLT systems, Redwood should not keep PII by default (they will send hashed customer IDs).
- Compliance: GDPR/CCPA concerns around transcripts; minimal retention + ability to delete.
- Fallback behavior: if Redwood hosted model latency spikes, they want graceful degrade to a lighter model or pass-through to a cached summary.

Technical notes / gotchas surfaced on call:
- Input format: CLT may send transcript chunks interleaved with metadata (agent_id, convo_id, customer_id_hashed). We need clear schema. Action: Sofia to propose stable JSON schema (see action items).
- Tokenization: Their front-end counts tokens differently; recommend we instrument token-estimates server-side to avoid user-visible truncation surprises. Miguel to add a metric for token-estimate delta.
- Real-time constraints: They prefer streaming partial summaries (word/phrase-level). Hosted API can stream, but we need to confirm whether Dedicated supports same streaming semantics. Rajan to confirm with Serving Runtime team.
- Region routing: They will need EU-only traffic for EU customers. Smart routing policy must support per-customer routing policy. This is standard but note: CLT also asked for per-route whitelist of regions.
- KMS: CLT uses AWS KMS with annual key-rotation. Private deployments must support BYOK/HSM. Note for sales: bring Private option after pilot.
- Rate limits: their internal rate limiter is permissive; they asked for higher burst capacity. Dedicated pools or reserved throughput recommended as path to production.

Initial architecture suggestion (pilot):
- Phase 0 (pilot, 6-8 weeks): Redwood Hosted API in EU region, use a medium-latency optimized model (e.g., open-llm-medium) with prefix caching for agent history; streaming responses to UI. Use webhook delivery for final summaries to CLT backend. Monitoring: latency SLO dashboard + token cost estimates.
- Phase 1 (post-pilot): Move to Dedicated pool with reserved capacity for peak concurrent agents; enable VPC peering + KMS integration for US customers. Consider Private deployment for full data isolation and BYOK if they decide.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Sofia: draft JSON request schema + sample payload examples by 2026-02-28. (JIRA: CS-4123)
- Rajan: confirm streaming semantics compatibility for Dedicated + Private with Serving Runtime team by 2026-03-04.
- Miguel: add token-estimate metric and token-delta alert in Sandbox by 2026-03-08.
- Priya (CLT): provide sample anonymized transcripts and expected routing logic by 2026-03-03.
- Solutions Eng (Sofia + Miguel): prepare pilot cost estimate + capacity plan for 6-8 week pilot by 2026-03-05.
- Sales: prepare deck comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private cost and SLA implications (linked PR for numbers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2147) by 2026-03-09.

Potential risks / questions to resolve:
- Latency SLO: 400ms 95th is aggressive for models + network; need experiment in staging with streaming enabled. If not achievable, propose a UX mitigation (showing live incremental summary with spinner and final commit).
- PII handling: CLT will send hashed IDs, but free-text user messages could contain PII. Need to confirm whether CLT wants server-side PII filter or will handle redaction client-side.
- Cost ramp: estimated tokens per summary currently uncertain; need sample transcripts to model cost. Prioritize getting sample data from Priya.

Notes / informal thoughts:
- Important to highlight streaming parity between Hosted and Dedicated; product should avoid feature-gap during their ramp. If Dedicated lacks streaming, that’s a blocker.
- We should offer a short-term experiment: enable prefix caching aggressively for repeated agent prompts to cut token costs for pilot.
- Consider pre-warming model shards for predictable p95 latency during scheduled peak windows (night shift in EU). This will be expensive but can be scoped into Dedicated offering.

Follow-ups scheduled:
- Quick sync (30m) w/ Priya + Rajan + Sofia on sample payloads and privacy flow on 2026-03-03 10:00 CET (Sofia to send invite).
- Internal technical review (45m) to review Dedicated streaming support w/ Serving Runtime on 2026-03-04 15:00 PST (Rajan organizing).

Reference links mentioned on call:
- Confluence onboarding page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CS/pages/682094/Cedar+Lane+Telecom+Onboarding
- JIRA: CS-4123 (pilot request + schema)
- Internal PR for cost calc: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2147

Quick checklist for next week (priority order):
1) Get sample transcripts from CLT (Priya).
2) Sofia drafts schema + sample payloads.
3) Run staging experiments for latency + streaming parity.
4) Produce pilot cost/capacity plan and present to CLT.

Notes-to-self: keep the ask visible in the EU-compliance backlog. If they push for Private earlier than expected, escalate to Jake + Legal for contract timing.

-- Rajan
